title:
Your face.
Someone else's ad.
caption: WHO GETS TO SAY YES?
voice: Imagine seeing your face in an ad you never agreed to. Someone else chose the message. Someone else got paid.

title:
Where was
your permission?
caption: CONSENT SHOULD COME FIRST
voice: Making that image keeps getting easier. Getting your permission should be just as simple.

title: Three missing pieces.
caption: PERMISSION  /  PAYMENT  /  PROOF
voice: Creators need a say in how their likeness is used. Brands need clear permission they can actually verify. And both need a record that connects the person, the agreement, and the finished image.

title: Facetime.
caption: YOUR FACE. YOUR TERMS.
voice: That's why we built Facetime. A creator chooses the terms. A brand requests a licence. Every paid render carries a receipt. And when the creator says stop, the next render has to stop too.

title: First, a real person.
caption: VERIFICATION · ANIMATED RECONSTRUCTION
voice: Here's the onboarding, illustrated. An identity check confirms an adult, with a live selfie and a face match.

title: Photos, protected.
caption: MATCH → ENCRYPT → STORE
voice: Three reference photos are matched, then encrypted in the browser with a key derived from your passkey.

title: Now, my actual account.
caption: ACTUAL LOCAL APP · REGISTERED CREATOR
voice: I've already completed registration, so let's move into my actual account. This is the creator dashboard running locally. You can see my verification, my licence settings, and the controls that stay with me.

title: I set the terms.
caption: 2 USDC / RENDER · APPROVAL REQUIRED
voice: My starting terms allow advertising and social use, worldwide, at two USDC per render. Each licence can last thirty days, with up to a hundred renders. And every request needs my approval.

title: A request, not a blank cheque.
caption: ILLUSTRATED WORKFLOW · BRAND REQUEST
voice: Now follow an example brand request. A coffee brand asks for five images for a social campaign. The request spells out the use, the duration, and the price, before the creator decides whether to approve.

title: Permission is specific.
caption: APPROVE → ISSUE LICENCE → RELEASE PHOTOS
voice: Approval signs that specific agreement. The brand issues the licence, and the creator releases the reference photos to the renderer for that licence. Having an account alone does not grant access to somebody's face.

title: Pay for each use.
caption: EXAMPLE · 10 USDC FUNDED / 2 USDC PER RENDER
voice: The brand deposits ten USDC into escrow. Each two USDC render pays one eighty to the creator and twenty cents to the platform. The remaining balance stays available for the licence, rather than becoming an unlimited buyout.

title: Check before creating.
caption: LOCAL DEMO · TEST RENDERER
voice: Before rendering, the service checks the licence, its limits, the available funds, and the prompt. This local setup uses a clearly marked test renderer. The generated image integration is separate from the consent and payment flow.

title: Proof. And a way to stop.
caption: RECEIPT → VERIFY → REVOKE
voice: A paid output gets a receipt and a content credential. The verifier connects it back to its licence. Revoke that licence, and future renders are refused. Earlier files remain traceable as licensed when made, since revoked.

title: One connected flow.
caption: IDENTITY → CONSENT → PAYMENT → PROVENANCE
voice: Under the hood, React and Next.js connect Dynamic wallets, Didit verification, Mera passkey encryption, and a Gemini render integration. Monad contracts hold licences, escrow, and receipts. C2PA carries provenance in the file. Reference photos stay encrypted in storage and are decrypted in memory for authorized rendering.

title: Built to be inspected.
caption: LOCAL MONAD FORK · TEST CREDENTIALS
voice: This demo runs on a local Monad fork, with test credentials. The next milestone is proving the full experience with production services and independently reviewed contracts.

title:
Your face.
Your terms.
caption: FACETIME · CONSENT THAT SOFTWARE CAN CHECK
voice: AI is changing what people can create. The people in those images should share in that value, and keep a say in what happens next. That's Facetime. We'd love to show you the controls behind it.
